title: A canonical digest for a pipe-inspection survey

blocks.text: A water utility's inspection team sends pipe surveys to a planning service, and both teams must be able to name a survey by its digest: the same survey content gives the same digest on either side, whatever order the keys or records arrive in. A survey has scalar fields, a list of `tags`, and a list of `segments`, each with an `id`, a `material`, a length and a list of wall-thickness `readings` taken in order along the pipe.
In `survey.py`, write `digest(doc)`: the SHA-256 hex digest of the survey's canonical bytes, defined by both teams as follows.

items: The records of `segments` are in `id` order, and `tags` are sorted. These are the lists named in `UNORDERED`. The rule goes by the key a list sits under, at any depth: a list held under a key named in `UNORDERED`, in any object of the document, is sorted the same way. Every other list, `readings` included, keeps its order.
Every float is cut to 3 decimals by fixed-point formatting, so `0.1 + 0.2` and `0.3` agree; `-0.0` becomes `0.0`; a NaN or an infinity raises `ValueError`.
The bytes are `json.dumps` of the result with sorted keys, separators `(",", ":")`, `ensure_ascii=True` and `allow_nan=False`, encoded as ASCII.

blocks.text: One segment's material is written with a non-ASCII letter, so the last rule matters: the other team has pinned the digest of the test survey, and only exactly these bytes give it. About twenty lines.

cases.says: the same survey with its keys in another order and another layout has the same digest; one changed reading changes it
segments listed in another order are the same survey
tags listed in another order are the same survey
readings are taken in order along the pipe, so reversing them is a different survey
0.1 + 0.2 and 0.3 are the same rate at three decimals
a rate of -0.0 is the rate 0.0
a rate of NaN has no canonical form and is refused with ValueError
the bytes are exactly the documented form, so the digest matches the one the other team pinned

origin.section: Hash the Validated Content in Canonical Form, Not the File

concepts: a digest of content in canonical form: sorted keys, only the order-free lists sorted, floats at a fixed precision, NaN refused, one documented byte form
